the-bar-raiser-mechanism.core: Amazon's Bar Raiser is a specially trained interviewer from outside the hiring team, with veto power, whose job is to ensure every hire is better than half the current people at that level. It counters the hiring manager's urgency bias and keeps standards consistent across the company.

first_principles.problem: Teams under pressure to fill seats lower the bar, and quality erodes over time.

analogy.title: An independent auditor
analogy.story: The company wants good numbers; the auditor ensures they meet the standard regardless.
analogy.breaks: Auditors check past records; bar raisers predict future performance.

example.title: A debrief
flow: Bar raiser: weak ownership evidence across 3 rounds

check.q: Why is the bar raiser outside the hiring team?
check.a: To avoid urgency and team biases, giving an independent judgement on long-term standards.

decoding-the-behavioral-rubric-lps-and-g.core: Behavioural rounds score against explicit rubrics: Amazon's Leadership Principles (Ownership, Dive Deep, Bias for Action…) or Google's 'Googleyness and Leadership' (comfort with ambiguity, collaboration, humility). Map your stories to the rubric so each answer clearly demonstrates the competency being assessed.

first_principles.problem: A good story fails because it doesn't show the specific principle the interviewer is scoring.
truths: Evidence must be specific and personal.
derivation: **Highlight** the behaviour explicitly ('I dove into the logs myself').

analogy.title: Answering an exam with the mark scheme in mind
analogy.story: You make sure each point the examiner looks for is clearly present.
analogy.breaks: Exams have fixed answers; rubrics reward authentic, specific stories, not keywords.

example.title: 'Dive Deep' story
flow: Metrics looked fine, but complaints rose
I sampled raw request logs myself
Found 2% of EU requests timing out

check.q: Why map stories to leadership principles?
check.a: Interviewers score specific competencies; explicit evidence makes your answer score clearly.

red-flag-not-invented-here-nih-syndrome.core: Not Invented Here syndrome is reflexively rebuilding things that already exist because external solutions feel inferior or untrusted. Interviewers treat it as a judgement red flag: it wastes resources and signals ego. Strong candidates evaluate existing options first and build only with clear justification.

first_principles.problem: A candidate proudly describes writing their own message queue for a CRUD app.
truths: Mature tools encode years of fixes.
Interviewers assess judgement, not just skill.

analogy.title: Building your own car to commute
analogy.story: Impressive engineering, but a terrible use of time when cars exist.
analogy.breaks: Sometimes no car fits your road, and justified builds are fine.

example.title: Reframing a story
flow: Weak: 'I built our own auth system'
Strong: 'We evaluated Auth0 and Keycloak; neither met our offline requirement, so we built a thin layer on Keycloak'

check.q: Why is NIH a red flag in interviews?
check.a: It signals poor judgement about cost, maintenance and business priorities.

the-hiring-committee-and-the-packet-revi.core: At companies like Google, a hiring committee that never met you decides from a written packet: interviewer feedback, scores, résumé and references. Clear, well-documented signal in each round matters, so think aloud, structure answers and make strengths easy for interviewers to write down.

first_principles.problem: A candidate who felt great in interviews is rejected because the written feedback was vague.
truths: Vague feedback reads as weak signal.
derivation: **Narrate** reasoning so it can be recorded.

analogy.title: A jury reading trial transcripts
analogy.story: They weren't in the room; only what was recorded counts.
analogy.breaks: Transcripts are verbatim; interviewer notes are summaries, so make key points memorable.

example.title: Making signal writable
flow: State approach and complexity before coding
example.outcome: a packet that argues for you.

check.q: Why does thinking aloud matter for committee-based hiring?
check.a: The committee only sees written feedback; narrated reasoning gives interviewers concrete evidence to record.
